blocks.content: Coriolis force is an apparent force caused by Earth's rotation that deflects moving objects such as winds and ocean currents.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Coriolis force is an apparent force resulting directly from Earth's rotation.
Objects like winds and ocean currents are deflected to the RIGHT in the Northern Hemisphere and to the LEFT in the Southern Hemisphere.
The force magnitude is ZERO at the Equator and reaches its Maximum at the poles.
Without the Coriolis effect, global wind systems and cyclones would fail to rotate.

blocks.content: Coriolis force is an apparent force caused by Earth's rotation that deflects moving objects such as winds and ocean currents.

items: Deflection direction is frequently tested: RIGHT in the Northern Hemisphere and LEFT in the Southern Hemisphere.
Magnitude variation questions: Remember that Coriolis force is ZERO at the Equator and Maximum at the poles.
Cyclonic rotation depends on Coriolis force; cyclones cannot form at the Equator due to zero Coriolis force.
